title: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II
platform: International Space Station, Microgravity Science Glovebox
summary: BASS-II (Burning and Suppression of Solids-II) was a set of small-scale solid-fuel burn tests run by astronauts in a small flow duct inside the Microgravity Science Glovebox on the ISS (mostly 2014), varying ambient O2 (about 13.6-22.2%), flow velocity (about 0.3-55 cm/s) and fuel type, thickness and shape (PMMA films, slabs and rods, SIBAL fabric, Nomex) to map flammability and extinction limits without buoyancy and compare with 1g. Captured as flammability limits stated by the PIs in NASA/TM-20210011385; the 129 individual runs are kept in data/raw/PSI-25.

normal_gravity_reference.note: Normal-gravity upward flame spread limit of 15.4% O2 with an added 4 cm/s forced flow (Ref. 23); below this upward burning is not sustained. Buoyant flow at flame base ~20 cm/s (Ref. 32) (p76, p89).

tests.notes: Minimum of the O2 vs stretch-rate flammability boundary, X_O2 = 6exp(-0.5a)+0.0167a+13.4 (Eq. 6.1; blowoff-branch intercept 13.4% extrapolated to a=0). Flow 2 cm/s is the stated diffusive velocity UD at which blowoff->quenching transition occurs (U/UD=1, p88), not a separately measured limit velocity, hence medium. Direction: authors call these concurrent-flow rod tests in axial stagnation flow (abstract, conclusions). Lowest-O2 test is O4 (O2 14.8->13.6%). Quote: "minimum O2 concentration of 13.5 percent O2 at a of 8 to 12 s–1". Pressure: report states 1 atm (pp. 11, 22, 28, 94); measured 99.2–99.5 kPa in the section 2.3 tests (p. 38). Open: Flow 2 cm/s is the diffusive velocity UD at the transition (also consistent with U = a r / 1.5 = 1.7-2.5 cm/s for a = 8-12 s-1, r = 0.318 cm), not a measured limit flow. Direction: abstract says concurrent; Appendix A.5 lists these tests as Stagnation. 13.5 is the fit/graph minimum; lowest measured final O2 with flame is 13.6 (O4).

tests.notes: Statement by Olson about the Fernandez-Pello opposed rod tests; conflicts with the 17.5% minimum stated in section 4 (p50). P8 (3/8 in. black rod, 16.4%, would not stay lit) matched by inferred by CSV match. Consistent with Fernandez-Pello: 17.5% (p50) is a comparison level, not a minimum. Quote: "opposed-flow flame spread was not observed below 16.4 percent O2 at any flow". Pressure: report states 1 atm (pp. 11, 22, 28, 94); measured 99.2–99.5 kPa in the section 2.3 tests (p. 38). Review: Statement by Olson about the Fernandez-Pello opposed rod tests. Not a contradiction of the 17.5% in section 4 (p50): that value is a comparison-level 'as low as', while spread was seen at 16.8% (P17) and none at or below 16.4% (P8, P21). P8 (3/8 in. = 9.525 mm black rod, 16.4% calibrated, tried at 5, 10 and 15 cm/s, 'would not stay lit') matches Olson's 'at any flow'; P21a/b (6.35 mm, 16.3%) are consistent evidence below 16.4%. Olson cites Ref. 14 but that reference is a sensor paper; the opposed rod tests are Fernandez-Pello's (Table A.3). Quote: "opposed-flow flame spread was not observed below 16.4 percent O2 at any flow". Pressure: report states 1 atm (pp. 11, 22, 28, 94); measured 99.2–99.5 kPa in the section 2.3 tests (p. 38). Open: Olson gives no run or diameter; P8 is chosen as the exact O2/flow match. The wording 'not observed below 16.4' can be read as limit just at/below 16.4%.

1.2 cm wide sample. Blowoff velocity taken as the final velocity (47 cm/s; CSV: 'max(47)'). Table 7.1 also lists 'No blowoff' for T15 (18.7% O2, up to 29 cm/s) and T17 (16.9%, up to 53 cm/s), which are lower bounds not limits; T17 not blowing off at 53 cm/s sits oddly with T21 blowing off at 47 cm/s (width and O2 differ). Quote: "GMT190-T21 1.2 11 to 47 17.2 Blow-off". Pressure: report states 1 atm (pp. 11, 22, 28, 94); measured 99.2–99.5 kPa in the section 2.3 tests (p. 38). Open: T17 (2.2 cm, 16.9%, 6 to 53 cm/s) did not blow off while T21 (1.2 cm, 17.2%) did at 47: different widths; not a data error. Appendix lists the sample as '1 cm SIBAL'.

2.2 cm wide samples did not ignite at 16.4% O2 (T9 at 10 cm/s, T10 at 5 cm/s) and 16.8% (T12 at 5 cm/s), whereas T14 and T17 ignited at 16.9%. The text says near the boundary ignition is sporadic and a decreasing-O2 procedure is needed (p100), so this is a bracket, not a sharp limit. Multiple flows so flow_velocity_cm_s is null. Quote: "GMT175-T9 2.2 10 16.4 No ignition". Pressure: report states 1 atm (pp. 11, 22, 28, 94); measured 99.2–99.5 kPa in the section 2.3 tests (p. 38). Open: Appendix A.6 notes show brief flashes at the igniter for T9/T10/T12 ('Extinguished quickly'), so 'no ignition' means no sustained flame. Bracket, not a sharp limit.
